note: Physical acceptance state for the MIDI Brain hardware. An item moves to "accepted" only with measured evidence in docs/evidence/ that names a reviewer, a date and the current hardware fingerprint. The fingerprint covers the canonical PCB/panel sources, the mechanical TS-to-CAD bridge and its exported layout, the CAD algorithm, the JLCPCB order settings and the curated cable/hardware selection, so any hardware, algorithm, order-setting or part-selection change makes old evidence stale. Refresh hardware_fingerprint with `bun run scripts/release_gate.ts --fingerprint` after such a change; a documentation-only commit does not change it. There is no override key: unknown keys are errors. See docs/acceptance.md.

items.note: Measured board, standoff, display, Pi, HAT, cooler and panel thicknesses that add up to a stack, with the installed depth recorded.

Knob, button caps and the 4-way nav actuator fitted and measured against the panel: shaft, detent, cap height and direction legends. NAV has been the THT ALPS Alpine RKJXT1F42001 since the 2026-11-14 owner decision, so this item also carries: (1) a meter check of every terminal pair before soldering - the pin numbers are the library's own (ALPS prints terminal names only), so confirm which physical post is which and that no unintended permanent connection exists; the ALPS page-399 output-relation chart is NOT ambiguous: `Push-Com` is ON in every lever position (directions and centre push alike), so every tilt grounds NAV_PRESS with its direction line, and the firmware decodes the five contacts as one group (`mb::NavPressGate`) so a tilt cannot select; (2) the collar diameter (D7.20, model geometry) and the housing tab height (9.00, one model) against the 8.2 mm NAV panel opening and the panel rear plane; (3) whether the printed push-on cap stays on the D2.50 flatted shaft - its retention is a press fit (D2.40 bore, 0.05 mm radial interference at nominal, no clip, screw or flange), so print a fit specimen and measure the grip, the rock and the binding. Include a sample continuity check on every fitted B3F-4055: the Omron B3F drawing (page 6) shows pins 1-2 internally common and 3-4 internally common with the switch opening/closing between those pairs, and the boards wire pin 1 to ground and pin 3 to the signal. That pairing is a source-design reading, not a sample measurement.
TRS jack (QingPu/Thonkiconn WQP419GR, M6 x 0.5) barrel, nut and 6.2 mm panel-hole fit, tip/ring/sleeve continuity and pull-out retention measured on the sample.

Fitted light pipe selected for the current 10.6 mm panel stack, its fitted length and the LED-to-pipe optical gap measured, and each of the three LEDs visible through its panel hole. No suitable part is selected today: the PGN25L165 candidate has a 16.5 mm shaft and would reach 5.9 mm behind the board face, so this item needs a ~9.8 mm-class part or a documented cut, and the part actually fitted is what gets measured.

Waveshare 4.3 inch DSI panel mounted on the printed carrier bolted to the rear board at the fitted SMTSO boss pattern, with a DSI cable that suits the run between the two modules (carrier on the rear board to the Pi on its own mounting panel) routed: bend radius and latch verified, display underside clearance recorded.

The fitted display mounting confirmed on the physical module: the SMTSO-M2.5 bosses (99.30 x 61.80 pattern) take the spacer screws and the 58.00 x 49.04 plain holes do not. The design values are NOMINAL: 12.75 mm from the rear board's front face to the display PCB rear face = 4.0 mm boss projection + 8.75 mm spacer, with the spacer EXTENDED (never cut) to about 9.35 mm to bring the glass flush. The evidence records the separation and the spacer length actually fitted, plus the real boss plane the spacer has to reach.

The display FPC plug, its latch and its first cable bend coexist with the carrier, the rear-board parts and the front board's 106.50 x 68.90 mm opening, with the routed bend per the route contract in docs/mechanical-stack.md and the clearance to the J5 female solder tails recorded. The 2 x 13 link is a direct male/female pair: no plug and no ribbon. No FPC connector position or clearance is established today (the recorded position is unverified planning data).

Direct 2 x 13 pair fitted and measured BEFORE any power is applied: front female Sullins SFH11-PBPC-D13-ST-BK on the front board's bottom face and rear male SBH11-PBPC-D13-ST-BK on the rear board's top face. The Pi is on its own mounting panel, so no board sits above the male tails: measure the tail/joint protrusion below the rear board and the fitted clearance around it. Seat-to-seat board gap measured against the 11.20 +-0.20 mm drawing dimension with the spacer/support recorded; centred polarizing key engaging in one orientation only; all 26 contacts continuity-tested pin for pin against the net list, each pair recorded separately; the 1.00 mm drill recorded as the male manufacturer recommendation and as a PROVISIONAL assumption for the female (no published female hole); the male's 3.00 mm solder tails recorded as a seating-face dimension (nominal 1.40 mm below a 1.60 mm PCB) with the fillet height and PCB tolerance measured. Hardware fit remains unverified.

The 20HP x 3U Pi mounting panel (101.2 x 128.5 mm bare FR-4) fitted beside the main module in the same row, with the Pi 5 (Active Cooler + M.2 HAT+ + NVMe SSD) bolted to its rear face on measured standoffs, and all six harness runs recorded end to end: the three USB feedthrough cables (5 A power feed droop and temperature included), the DSI FPC extension (cable, 15 to 22 pin adaptation, touch and signal integrity over the fitted length), the 40-wire GPIO ribbon to J_PI (pin-1, all-40 continuity, coexistence with the M.2 HAT+'s GPIO use) and the J_PWR pigtail to the bare J2 pads. Nothing is measured today, including both modules' installed depth.
The delivered display module label/SKU read and matched the selected part (Waveshare 4.3inch DSI LCD, ElectroKit 4103 5687) that the drawing and STEP model were sourced from.

With the display seated in the 107.22 x 68.87 panel window, touch input stays aligned with the visible UI: glass centred in the cutout and touch coordinates agree with the active-area silkscreen window.
microSD card inserted and removed with the Pi in the stack and the case closed; recorded clearance.
Active Cooler, M.2 HAT+ and NVMe SSD stacked and measured for height, airflow path and connector clearance.

30HP/3U panel (152.0 mm actual), the 148 x 112 mm rear/base board, the 20HP/3U Pi mounting panel (101.2 mm actual) and every rail and standoff position fitted in the rack case at the recorded installed depth, for both modules.
An exact 5 A rated panel feedthrough selected from a primary source (CAB-15455 is 3 A and rejected for this path) with the rating recorded.
Full-load PD negotiation, cable voltage droop and connector/feedthrough temperature measured in both orientations.
Bourns PEC11R process qualified: selective/wave soldering or a validated manual process with recorded profile and inspection.

J_PWR as the right-angle Harwin M20-9960245 on the front board's rear (bottom) face at x = 64 mm, y = 44.5 mm, rotation 180, mating axis +Y into the 11.20 mm board gap; there is no top relief notch and no part sits in one. The printed bracket carries a pocket for it, and the mating plug is a provisional generic 2.54 mm DuPont-style female (no measured size). PLACED: imports/M20_9960245.tsx from POWER_HEADER in tscircuit/lib/layout.ts; the bracket pocket (x 59.69...68.31, y 41.96...56, inside the bar) is cut by mechanical/feedthrough_bracket.py, whose self-check reports one connected solid and no material inside the declared POWER_HEADER_KEEPOUT over its 4.80 mm height. The exact hole-to-housing offset is UNRESOLVED (the 4.80 mm datum is unclear, sheet 1 of 2 missing), so the keepout is an envelope, not a part; the 1.60 mm pad and 8.00 mm plug reach are engineering assumptions; the plug is generic; UMC AUDIO cable access in the same slot is unverified; the printed pocket fit is unproven. Sourcing: the DigiKey listing was observed once in a live browser with no committed snapshot and digikey.se returns Cloudflare 403 to scripted clients, so stock is subject to reconfirmation, this is a checked-date source lead and not an approved DigiKey source, and the Electrokit breakaway strip is not selected. The Pi end is NOT a connector: the Raspberry Pi documentation power-button page (with its official images/j2.jpg) shows J2 as TWO BARE PADS between the RTC battery connector and the board edge, so a female DuPont jumper cannot connect there; a correctly fitted header or a qualified wired connection is required, with exact pitch, part, clearance, insulation and assembly method pending, dry-contact only, and no JST-SH or pad pitch assumed. Evidence must record the measured housing offset, the plug housing and cable bend, the pocket print and fit, the UMC AUDIO tail coexistence, switch continuity from SW7 through J_PWR to the Pi end BEFORE power, that each fitted B3F-4055 closes between its 1-2 and 3-4 common pairs (Omron B3F drawing page 6, a source reading), that SW7 is open at rest, and soldering/plugging access. Hardware fit pending.
Measured receiver threshold against the MIDI CA-033 <5 mA requirement at the recorded supply and temperature.

TLP2361 input current and junction temperature measured at worst-case high-rail/low-VF source corners, with the recorded ambient: recommended 2-6 mA, absolute continuous 10 mA at 25 C derated -0.13 mA/C above 110 C (8.05 mA at 125 C), and the 220 ohm choice justified by measurement.

Measure low-rail transmitter current into legacy receiver loads, rise/fall below 2 us and sustained ring/tip fault temperatures. The output topology and any deviation from the CA-033 reference need independent review; receiver threshold analysis alone cannot close this item.
Two real MIDI devices (not loopback) exchange note, clock and sysex traffic in both directions with the recorded equipment.

Short, open, reverse and over-current cases on both MIDI inputs and outputs measured against the protection parts. The analysis covers the board rail only: an externally driven +-12 V mispatch on a MIDI input or output is NOT modelled, so no survival and no exact fault current may be claimed. The owner must choose the voltage/fault-survival requirement first, because that test can be destructive.
Logic-analyser or scope capture of SPI0 clock/data and READY at the target rate, including the Pico USB and Pi-off cases.

Power-up and power-down order for Pi, Pico, display and 3.3 V rails captured with no backfeed or latch-up. Include the Pi powered with the Pico unpowered and with the Pico absent: that case is not assumed safe and its behaviour must be measured.
Closed-rack thermal soak at the recorded ambient and load, with cooler noise and NVMe temperature recorded.

With the assembly state recorded for each measurement (front board fitted or off, Pi fitted or removed, Pico socketed, Pico USB cable fitted or not), every rear-board probe point TP1-TP15 reached with the intended probe and read on the net the board declares; the pad, the side used, the assembly state and any obstruction recorded. In-rack access is not assumed.

Abrupt removal and re-application of power recorded on the full stack: rail decay order and time captured, Pico/Pi/display state, write integrity of the microSD card or NVMe SSD after a loss during a recording, and any backfeed or latch-up seen. No graceful-shutdown behaviour is assumed.
JLCPCB DFM/order-preview review of copper, mask, silkscreen, drill and CPL rotation on the engineering prototype material, with findings recorded.
The tscircuit warning 'Could not save autorouting paths' resolved, or its effect on the routed copper reviewed and recorded.
First-article boards built, inspected and tested against the acceptance list before any production order.
